summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree: big-O notation, a first course in discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, gcd, primes, binomial coefficients, induction, radix representation, Boolean logic), a first linear algebra course (vector spaces, subspaces, dimension, linear maps and kernels, rank, elimination, invertible and triangular matrices, eigenvalues, projections, orthogonality for the dot product), and calculus-level analysis (logarithms, geometric series, Newton's method). They have not studied tensor products, general bilinear forms, Gaussian or dyadic rings, Chinese remainder theorem, Bruhat factorizations, or the transform theory beyond the discrete Fourier transform.

known.name: Vector space, subspace and dimension
known.gloss: A vector space over a field is closed under addition and scalar multiplication; a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space, and its dimension is the size of any basis.

known.name: Linear map, kernel and image
known.gloss: A linear map sends a vector space to another preserving addition and scalar multiplication; its kernel is the set sent to zero and its image the set of outputs, with dim(image) + dim(kernel) equal to the dimension of the domain.

known.name: Invertible matrix
known.gloss: A square matrix A is invertible when some matrix B satisfies AB = BA = I; equivalently it has full rank and nonzero determinant.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Gaussian elimination reduces a matrix to row echelon form by swapping rows and adding multiples of one row to another, and the pivot positions it finds determine the rank.

known.name: Triangular and permutation matrices
known.gloss: A lower-triangular matrix has zeros above its diagonal and an upper-triangular one has zeros below; a permutation matrix has exactly one 1 in each row and in each column and zeros elsewhere.

known.name: Matrix multiplication and transpose
known.gloss: The product of conformable matrices has entries given by row-by-column dot products, and the transpose of a matrix is obtained by interchanging its rows and columns.

known.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
known.gloss: A scalar λ is an eigenvalue of a square matrix A when Av = λv for some nonzero vector v, which happens exactly when λ is a root of det(A − λI).

known.name: Projection and direct sum decomposition
known.gloss: A linear map P with P² = P is a projection; if V = U ⊕ W then P is the projection onto U along W, fixing U and sending W to zero.

known.name: Orthogonal complement
known.gloss: For a subspace U of R^n under the standard dot product, its orthogonal complement is the set of vectors whose dot product with every vector of U is zero.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residue classes
known.gloss: Two integers are congruent modulo n when they differ by a multiple of n; arithmetic on residue classes is well defined, and a residue has a multiplicative inverse exactly when it is coprime to n.

known.name: Field of two elements
known.gloss: The integers modulo 2, a field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is exclusive or (XOR) and multiplication is AND.

known.name: Logic gates and circuits
known.gloss: A logic gate computes a Boolean function of its input bits such as AND, OR, NOT or XOR, and a circuit is a network of such gates that computes a function by composition.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and extended Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, computed by Euclid's algorithm, whose extended form also finds integers x and y with ax + by = gcd(a, b).

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient C(n,k) is the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set, equal to n!/(k!(n-k)!).

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for every natural number by proving a base case and showing that the statement for smaller cases implies it for the next.

known.name: Positional radix representation
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer written in radix b as a finite sum of digits times powers of b, with binary being the case b = 2.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer at most x and the ceiling is the smallest integer at least x.

known.name: Logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which the base b must be raised to give x, and the natural logarithm and exponential function are inverse to one another with base e.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: For r not equal to 1, the sum of a r^j over j from 0 to k equals a(1 - r^(k+1))/(1 - r).

known.name: Recurrence relations and unrolling
known.gloss: A recurrence defines a sequence by a relation between its terms, and it is solved by repeatedly substituting the relation into itself until a closed-form bound appears.

known.name: Big-Omega, big-Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: f = Omega(g) means f is at least a positive constant times g for all sufficiently large inputs, f = Theta(g) means both f = O(g) and f = Omega(g), and f = o(g) means f/g tends to zero.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: Newton's method approximates a root of a differentiable function by iterating x ← x − f(x)/f'(x), converging rapidly when started near a simple root.

known.name: Polar form of complex numbers
known.gloss: Every nonzero complex number can be written r(cos θ + i sin θ) = r e^(iθ) with modulus r and argument θ, using Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ.

known.name: Permutation of a finite set
aliases: bijection of a set to itself
known.gloss: A permutation of a finite set is a bijection from the set to itself, and every permutation can be written as a composition of transpositions.
